questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A crucial aspect of choosing my study destination was the culture and the city, however it was also very important for me that the university had a profile that matched my expectations, offered courses that were relevant and interesting for my education and also offered different social activities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad experience was definitely one of the best experiences in my life, but sometimes it was also hard to be so far away from home. Also I didn't find accommodation before I arrived, and I had some problems with finding accommodation when I arrived, which effected the beginning of my stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was very easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university offered a free airport pickup, and there where a lot of assistance available in orientation week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A lot of people had recommended to not finding accommodation before my arrival in order to be able to inspect the accommodation before accepting it. However it was almost impossible to find something when I arrived, and everything was very expensive. But I can recommend using the app flatmates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very hard to find something and there is so many people who are looking for something.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is student accommodation available through the university, but I didn't choose this because it was very expense, and wanted to live a more social place. I ended up finding something cheaper and a very nice place, but it was hard and frustrating to find.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was a quite long proces.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to complete an application form, and upload different documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a contact person both at my home university and my destination university, but it took a long time for them to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was very easy and succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To set a lot of time aside to it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was great, and the lectures were very nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to take a lot of first year courses, but they were great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In some ways it was quite similar, but it was also more practical which was quite nice. Also I didn't have any exams, but instead we were graded on participation and different assessments through the whole semester. I found this way of grading the students very meaningful, and enjoyed it more than exams. This takes away some of the pressure that exams put on students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMU 1052 - Intro strategic communication
DRAM 1100 - The theatre experience 
DRAM 2025 - European theatre (1500-1800) 
DRAM 2030 - Experimentation in 20'th century theatre

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the courses were great, but I would especially recommend "intro strategic communication" and "Experimentation in 20'th century theatre".

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to live on a hostel for one month, and then I had to buy duvet, pillows, towels, plate, cup, cutlery etc. when I found my accommodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and alcohol

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs and activities to be a part of, and they also had a club that planned trips and parties for exchange students which was great. There was a club for almost everything, surfing, beach volley, tennis, drama, choir, music, art etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely "Quest"(Queensland University Exchange Students Society). We were on two weekend trips, with different activities, parties etc, and then they arranged different parties throughout the semester. This was a great club to be a part of, since you could meet other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
For activities in Brisbane I recommend: 
City beach, Felons, Eat Street, Mt Coot-tha Lookout. 

For daily trips from Brisbane I would really recommend: 
Gold Coast, Moreton Island, North Stradbroke Island, Sunshine Coast

For longer trips and holidays I recommend: 
Cairns, Sydney, Melbourne, Tasmania

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone is so nice, so just be open ad welcoming and don't be afraid to approach or talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How welcoming, polite and helpful everyone was.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of academic support available at the library. 

Become a part of QUEST.

Make sure to look in the lake at the university - it has five turtles.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social bond with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Being on exchange is not easy, everything is new, you are alone a lot, everything is in english, and you are very far away from home, family and friends but it is definitely worth it. It is a great adventure and you learn a lot from it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
